_schema: Ben's review queue. Canonical store; NEEDS_REVIEW.md is the readable mirror. Entry fields: id, title, raised (ISO date), kind, status, source, what, why_it_matters, options (array, only where there is a genuine fork), recommendation, files, resolution (null until Ben answers).
_note: Companion to backlog.json and review.json, NOT a replacement for either.
PURPOSE: things awaiting BEN'S JUDGEMENT. Three kinds live here:
- 'question'        — an open call nobody has made yet, usually surfaced by
doing adjacent work. Not blocking, or it would be a
backlog item with blocked_on set.
- 'decision-taken'  — a call made ON BEN'S BEHALF so work could continue.
Recorded here so it can be OVERTURNED rather than
quietly becoming precedent. This is the important half:
an unrecorded delegated decision is indistinguishable
from a decision Ben made.
- 'observation'     — something noticed in passing that is too small or too
cross-cutting to file, but which a human should see.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM review.json: review.json is a BLOCKER list — items blocked
on a visual artifact only Ben can produce (a mockup, an annotated screenshot).
Work there cannot proceed at all. Entries here are not blocking; they are
questions and reversible calls. If an entry turns out to need a mockup, move it
to review.json and leave a resolution here pointing at it.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM backlog.json: an entry here is not work. If Ben's answer
creates work, file a backlog item and resolve the entry with that item's id.
LIFECYCLE (revised 2026-08-14, Ben's ruling): this file is TRANSIENT — a live
queue of open calls, not a permanent audit trail. Append entries as they arise
and set status to 'resolved' with a resolution once answered, exactly as before.
But do NOT let resolved entries accumulate: prune them promptly rather than
holding them for posterity. The reasoning is not lost — it lands in code
comments, an authority doc, or a backlog item's design field at the moment the
work happens, and THAT is the durable record. Ben's own framing: 'the docs
should preserve changes made, and the review queue should only be for things
of that level of importance' — i.e. open and unresolved, not a history of
everything ever decided. A large housekeeping sweep this date closed 231
entries down to 2 genuinely open ones on this basis.
SEEDED 2026-08-01 at Ben's request, populated from that session.

items.title: Re-stress generation and time-lapse feel when playable
items.what: Ben wants to re-stress-test world generation and the staged-generation time-lapse once the game is playable, to judge whether it feels alive rather than just correct. RULING 2026-08-13 (Ben, elicitation form): keep open until playable - not scheduled, not folded into another item.

items.title: BL-404 was measured rather than implemented, and the measurement blocked it — a design call is owed
items.what: You asked for BL-404 next. It is NOT implemented, deliberately. Building the measurement first (tools/verify/interbody_pull_harness.cpp, now in the ctest tier) showed the fix I had recommended in the item cannot be written: `inject_interbody_demand` reads ONE of the home body's 17 markets as though it were the whole body. That market carries 12% of the body's demand, and a share of its supply that differs by toolchain — 1491 of 7498 on the MSVC build, 0 of 2863 on g++, same seed. So 'net against the previous tick's supply' silences 33% of the pull on one build and 0% on the other. Filed the underlying defect as BL-406 (the home market is an arbitrary pick) and made BL-404 require it.
items.why_it_matters: Three things need your call, and none of them are mine to take because they all move prices. (1) BL-406's fix: aggregate over the body (truest, multiplies the pull ~8x, needs pull_fraction re-tuned, outpost prices move), name a primary market per body (cheap, stable, keeps today's magnitude, but keeps 'the body's demand' meaning one market's), or pull per-counterpart-market (most faithful, largest, needs machinery that does not exist). (2) BL-404's own a/b/c, which should be decided in the same pass since aggregating changes what netting does. (3) Whether outpost prices are allowed to move now at all, or whether this waits behind BL-381 giving demand real weight. I have left both items open and resumable rather than picking.
options: BL-406 (a) aggregate over the home body + re-tune pull_fraction, and settle BL-404's netting in the same pass (recommended)
BL-406 (b) store a primary_market per body — cheap and stable, keeps current magnitudes, defers the meaning question
BL-406 (c) per-counterpart-market pull — most faithful to a trade model, largest change
Hold both until BL-381 (what supply and demand mean) lands, since the netting question is downstream of it
items.recommendation: Option (a), with BL-404 decided alongside it. But if outpost prices moving is unwelcome right now, (b) is a clean stopgap that makes the pick authored instead of accidental and costs almost nothing.
